answer: Startup bonds are the mechanism: before an agent can bid or vote, it locks collateral on-ledger sized to the capital it wields, so each identity carries a real balance at risk. The gate prices accounts instead of counting them. An attacker wanting a lagoon of synthetic identities must post that bond per sybil, locked for months, so the war chest scales with the number of personas. Bonds are slashed on collusion findings, while honest agents recover theirs on exit. Forging a mesa costs more than the attestation it buys, and no copper of earned reputation transfers, so fakes cannot be resold.
